title: Follow-up to Log-Linear Scaling: Is There Evidence of a Compute Cliff Above 100M Tokens?

original_idea.body:
# Follow-up to Log-Linear Scaling: Is There Evidence of a Compute Cliff Above 100M Tokens?

**Problem:** AISI measured scaling up to 100M tokens and found no plateau. Extrapolating upward: at what token budget (if any) would performance plateau? Is there evidence of diminishing returns above 100M tokens, or does the log-linear trend continue to arbitrarily high compute?

**Direction:** Using AISI's published data points, fit multiple growth models (log-linear, logistic/sigmoid, power law) and compare AIC/BIC fit statistics. The best-fit model implies whether a plateau exists and when. Test predictions at the next token budget tier (500M tokens if API costs permit) using a simplified challenge set (5-10 challenges). Compare against model predictions.

**Why it matters:** If the log-linear trend plateaus below human expert levels, there is a natural capability ceiling that prevents fully autonomous attacks. If it continues indefinitely, capability growth is bounded only by economic cost (currently ~$400 for 500M tokens) — a much more alarming trajectory.

**Relevant context:** AISI (arxiv 2603.11214): log-linear scaling, 10M→100M tokens, 59% gain, no plateau observed. Growth model fitting is standard statistical practice. Token budget cost: 100M tokens ~$80 (Opus 4.6), so 500M tokens ~$400 — feasible for a research study. This is a direct follow-up to the most important AISI finding.
